item.title: What Solidarity Looks Like - Teny Oded Gross & Andrew V. Papachristos - Inquest
item.description: A collaboration between the Institute for Nonviolence Chicago and Northwestern University is helping to save lives by honoring multiple forms of expertise.

item.title: A Path Forward - Dawn Poindexter - Inquest
item.description: After losing my son to gun violence, I started interviewing people who had taken a life in order to understand how we were trapped in the same cycles of suffering—and how we could heal.

item.title: Punishing Through Bureaucracy - Ivan Kilgore - Inquest
item.description: An obscure policy claimed to reward me for doing the work of rehabilitation—by sending me back to a high-security prison.

item.title: The Endless Punishment - Joshua Manson - Inquest
item.description: A recent book contributes firsthand testimony on the violence of solitary confinement and helps frame the question of why it has proven so central to mass incarceration.

item.title: “We have journalists every place in the world except in prisons.” - Christopher Blackwell - Inquest
item.description: Incarcerated journalist Christopher Blackwell discusses his recent book on solitary confinement, and what it would take to level the playing field for incarcerated writers.

item.title: The Oscars in Solitary Confinement - Seth Stern, Jeremy Busby & Corinne Shanahan - Inquest
item.description: ‘The Alabama Solution’ might win an Academy Award this weekend. Meanwhile, its incarcerated filmmakers are in lockdown because there’s no legal protections for imprisoned whistleblowers.

item.title: Inside Georgia’s Youth Detention Crisis - Jadelynn Zhang - Inquest
item.description: Even as crime falls in Georgia, the state pours vast resources into abusive youth facilities that disproportionately harm Black children, according to our investigation.

item.title: Public Defense Goes to the Capitol - Sharone R. Mitchell, Jr. - Inquest
item.description: Resource-strapped public defenders can usually only provide direct client services. Meanwhile, police and prosecutors get to lobby for legislative changes. In Illinois, we are upending that status quo.

item.title: Building Narrative Power - Daniel K. Forkkio with Adam McGee - Inquest
item.description: By giving formerly incarcerated people the resources to tell their stories through film, Represent Justice is showing how storytelling has a central role to play in decarceral work.

item.title: Inside America’s Most Secretive Supermax Prison - Eric King - Inquest
item.description: ADX federal prison is designed to hold people in extreme deprivation. Despite this, the men imprisoned there continue to fight for their rights and freedom.
